headline: High-risk workspace asymmetry: Devin can write and exfiltrate while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and undocumented for pairwise interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and Devin, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Devin can use MCP, files, and browser-based workflows, so if the zoomcamp content is manually copied into Devin or placed in a shared workspace, instruction-like content could be misread. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not observed.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp content is copied into Devin's workspace or MCP inputs
IF a shared filesystem or chat bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the zoomcamp repo and Devin workspace separate
Disable copy-paste of untrusted course text into agent prompts
Add a provenance note to any imported text
Review MCP inputs before enabling them
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging across bridges

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin has broad network egress, filesystem access, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens, while the zoomcamp profile exposes no sensitive data classes and no egress. The pairwise leakage risk is mainly from Devin exporting whatever it reads from shared files or integrations; the exact shared data path is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Devin's cloud workspace
IF Devin is connected to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion with real project data
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared repo clones
Rotate any tokens before connecting integrations
Restrict Devin to a non-sensitive test repository
Audit outbound destinations in the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on integration egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write files, modify git state, and run parallel sessions with shared integrations, while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and has no write surfaces. There is no direct write-write conflict evidenced between the pair, but if the course repo is used as a mutable workspace, Devin's git and filesystem writes can collide with human or external edits. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable git repository
IF external edits occur while Devin runs parallel sessions
mitigations: Assign Devin a separate branch
Freeze the repo during agent runs
Use pull-request review before merge
Limit Devin to read-only access on shared repos
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a planner-executor that can act autonomously and write to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, and Notion, so if it consumes outputs derived from the zoomcamp material, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The zoomcamp profile itself is a course repo with no execution surface, so the main risk is Devin treating imported content as authoritative. This is plausible but not directly documented for the pair.
conditions: IF Devin uses zoomcamp-derived text as source material for commits or tickets
IF Devin is allowed to act without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human approval before external actions
Mark imported course text as untrusted
Ask Devin to cite source links in outputs
Limit write permissions on integrations
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: The zoomcamp profile is open-source course material with no touched data classes, while Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent that handles repo keys and integration tokens. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operational policy gaps around secrets and logs. The other agent is not cited for a residency issue because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Devin's workspace
IF workspace logs retain secrets or personal data beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review retention settings for integrations
Avoid storing secrets in course materials
Use a separate workspace for compliance-sensitive work
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
